title: 3.9.2 Group PA Part 2: Build It
description: Turn the chart you just passed into five documented functions and a short main section. Eleven checks, all of them things Chapter 3 taught. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Fill in the header
steps.instructions: The top of script.js has three comment lines waiting: Problem, Partners, Date. Fill all three in. Both partners' names, on the Partners line, before anything else happens.

steps.title: Copy your contracts in as comments
steps.instructions: Your contract table from 3.9.1, one function per line as // comments: name, what goes in, what comes back. Do this before you write a single line of JavaScript. If a contract does not say what you meant on the chart, fix the wording now.

steps.title: Declare the seed data and the level
steps.instructions: Your list as an array of objects -- every record has the same three fields, in the same order. The threshold you compare against never changes, so it is a const in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
hints: Snack Shack: [{ name: 'Popcorn', price: 3.5, qty: 12 }, ...]
UPPER_SNAKE_CASE means REORDER_LEVEL, not reorderLevel
Every record in the array needs the same three properties -- 3.5.3 is the shape

steps.title: Write makeItem
steps.instructions: The function from the top of your contract table. It takes the same three values the record holds, builds an object literal with those properties, and returns it. Nothing prints.
hints: return { name: name, price: price, qty: qty }; -- 3.5.3
A function that prints instead of returning is the 3.2.13 error
Call it once at the bottom of the file so you can see it work

steps.title: Write totalValue
steps.instructions: An accumulator set to 0 before the loop, added to inside the loop, returned after it. §3.3.5 walks the list; §3.3.9 is the sum pattern. §3.7 has no method that combines a list into one value -- 3.7.19 only names the one that does. Do this by hand.
hints: let total = 0;  for (const item of list) { total = total + item.price * item.qty; }  return total;
An accumulator is 'a variable set before a loop and updated inside it' -- 3.3.9 is the worked example

steps.title: Write lowStock
steps.instructions: Start with an empty array, walk the list, and push the records that pass the comparison. Return the new array. §3.7 does not teach the method that does this -- 3.7.19 only names it -- so build it by hand, exactly as 3.3.13 does.
hints: const short = [];  for ... if (...) { short.push(item); }  return short;
push adds to the END of the array -- 3.3.2
This one must NOT change the list it was handed

steps.title: Write receiptLines
steps.instructions: One line per record, in the shape your problem statement gives. This is the one place §3.7 DOES hand you a tool: the map() method, given an arrow function as its callback (3.7.2, 3.4.12).
hints: return list.map((item) => item.name + ' x' + item.qty);
map() builds a NEW array -- the original is untouched (3.7.4)
The arrow is the callback: 3.4.8 is the shorthand rules

steps.title: Write sellItem
steps.instructions: Find the record whose name matches, lower its count by one, never below zero. This function is REQUIRED to change the list it was handed -- the caller holds the same array (3.6.2), so the change is already made when the function returns. Say so in a comment.
hints: Walk the list, find the record, change its property -- 3.6.3 is the worked example
Never below zero: 3.2.12 is the guard-clause shape
The function may return nothing at all -- the caller already has the changed list

steps.title: Write saveStock and loadStock
steps.instructions: Save: the list goes to localStorage as JSON text under a key you choose (3.8.15). Load: read the key back. A key that was never saved reads as null -- return the seed list then (3.8.15). Text you did not write can fail to parse, and 3.8.12 says what to do about it: do not let a bad value throw.
hints: localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list)); -- 3.8.4
const text = localStorage.getItem(KEY);  if (text === null) { ... } -- 3.8.15
Wrap the parse in try/catch -- 3.8.13 is the worked example

steps.title: Write the main section
steps.instructions: Below the functions, five to eight lines that CALL each one in order and print the results: the total, the low-stock list, the receipt lines, one sale, one save and one load. The functions do the work; this section only arranges the calls. Copy the order from your chart.

steps.title: Read it back to each other
steps.instructions: Swap the keyboard. The partner who did not type reads the program out loud, one function at a time, while the other checks it against the contract table. Every function on the chart should appear once. Fix what does not match, then run three sets of numbers through it -- you will need them for the demo writeup.

requirements.title: Both partners named in the header
requirements.description: The Partners line at the top of script.js has names on it
requirements.hint: Line 3 of script.js: // Partners: -- put both names after the colon.

requirements.title: The problem is named in the header
requirements.description: The Problem line says which of the four menu problems this is
requirements.hint: Line 2 of script.js: // Problem: -- Snack Shack, Lap Times, Seed Tray, or Library Cart.

requirements.title: The level is an UPPER_SNAKE_CASE const
requirements.description: The threshold that never changes is declared with const in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
requirements.hint: const REORDER_LEVEL = 5; -- capitals and underscores, and const rather than let, because it never changes.

requirements.title: A named function is declared
requirements.description: At least one function is declared with the function keyword, the way 3.1.2 teaches
requirements.hint: function totalValue(list) { -- the function keyword, a name, and the parameters it takes.

requirements.title: A function returns a value
requirements.description: At least one function hands a value back with return, rather than printing it
requirements.hint: return total; -- 3.2.9. Printing is not returning (3.2.13): the value has to reach the caller.

requirements.title: The data is an array of record objects
requirements.description: The seed data is an array whose elements are object literals with the same properties
requirements.hint: const stock = [{ name: 'Popcorn', price: 3.5, qty: 12 }, ...]; -- square brackets around a list of { objects }.

requirements.title: A loop walks the list
requirements.description: A for or for...of loop is present, the way 3.3.5 teaches
requirements.hint: for (const item of list) { -- the for...of form from 3.3.5, or the counted form.

requirements.title: push builds a new list
requirements.description: A new array is built up with the push method
requirements.hint: short.push(item); -- 3.3.2. The lowStock array starts empty and grows.

requirements.title: map() is called with an arrow function
requirements.description: The map method is given an arrow function as its callback
requirements.hint: list.map((item) => item.name + ' x' + item.qty) -- 3.7.2 for the method, 3.4.6 for the arrow.

requirements.title: Spread copies a record
requirements.description: A new object or array is built from an old one with the spread operator, the way 3.7.14 teaches
requirements.hint: return { ...item }; -- 3.7.15 is the worked example: 'everything in the old one', then any changes.

requirements.title: Data is saved and loaded
requirements.description: localStorage is used with JSON in both directions, the way 3.8.15 teaches
requirements.hint: localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(list)) in one function; JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)) in the other -- 3.8.15.
